claims.text: Thermal-expansion mismatch during composite solidification produces thermal stresses in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal-expansion mismatch and the resulting thermal stresses are the primary causes of the unresolved stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal-expansion mismatch and the resulting thermal stresses are the primary causes of the unresolved thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material is polycrystalline.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr material may be a composite.
Thermal stresses cause dislocation formation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermal stresses alter dislocation interactions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Thermally induced dislocation formation and interaction change the alloy's stress–strain behavior.
Thermally induced dislocation formation and interaction change the alloy's thermoelastic behavior.
Thermal stress increases as temperature increases.
Dislocation density increases as temperature increases.
The temperature-induced increases in thermal stress and dislocation density alter the alloy's mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The conditions extend to 1250 °C (1523 K), while the stated boundary ends at 1250 K (about 977 °C), so the proposed temperature limit excludes part of the stated test regime and the cited 1250 °C creep condition.
